text:
alexandra: Heads-up — Nimbus Health returned their vendor security questionnaire this morning. Main asks: data residency for inference cache, KMS/HSM support for Private, and a full subprocessors list. They flagged retention of KV cache and asked if we ever write prompt text to disk.

mike: Thanks. Can you drop the exact Qs? I can craft a concise response for them.

alexandra: Copy of the relevant snippet from their form:
```
- Do you persist model KV cache or request prompts to disk? If so, retention period?
- Describe encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options for Private deployments.
- List all subprocessors involved in processing or storing customer content.
```

solutions-eng-raj: TL;DR answer we should give: KV cache is in-memory by default (ephemeral), we do not persist raw prompts to disk for hosted inference. For Private deployments customers can opt into local disk persistence for performance — that's clearly called out in the Private ops guide and requires explicit config + controls. For encryption: we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) via major cloud KMS and can integrate with HSM in on-prem packages. Subprocessors: AWS/GCP/Azure (regional infra), Akamai (CDN), LogOps partner (log retention + access controls). I can draft a template paragraph.

legal-samantha: Please do not name the third-party vendor "LogOps" without contract review. We maintain a canonical subprocessors list (see link) and require customers to sign the DPA addendum when Private includes third-party logging. Also: provide our SOC 2 Type II summary and statement about not persisting PII in audit logs. I'll prep a redline-safe paragraph.

cso-bot: DPA intake ticket created: DPA-8712. Owner assigned: ellie.

ellie: I'll coordinate a quick screen-share with Nimbus tomorrow 11am PT to walk through the answers and optional Private package. @legal-samantha can you confirm the DPA addendum draft by EOD? @solutions-eng-raj can you paste the template text here so I can send it after legal sign-off?

solutions-eng-raj: Template below — feel free to copy/edit:
```
Redwood Inference response:
- KV cache and model working state: By default, KV cache is maintained in-memory on serving nodes and is ephemeral. Hosted inference does not persist full request/response bodies to disk.
- Optional persistence: Private customers may enable disk-backed persistence for caching/throughput; this requires explicit configuration and is subject to contractual controls.
- Encryption at rest and KMS: Redwood supports CMEK using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for hosted/dedicated. For Private/on-prem we support integration with customer HSM/KMS solutions; key management remains under customer control when configured.
- Subprocessors: Redwood engages cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure) and CDN/caching partners. A current list and data flow diagram are attached in the DPA packet.
```

legal-samantha: Suggested edits: remove vendor nicknames, add: "Audit logs capture request IDs, timestamps, and model identifiers; they do not store full prompt text unless explicitly enabled by the customer." Also, replace "attached" with a link to the canonical subprocessors doc. I uploaded SOC2 summary here: https://redwood-internal/reports/soc2-summary-2025.pdf

alexandra: Perfect. I'll wait on legal sign-off then send the short FAQ + SOC2 link to Nimbus. ellie will run the call and confirm whether Nimbus wants Private trial or hosted with VPC options.

tom: Action items: 1) raj — final template by EOD (1759004000) 2) samantha — DPA addendum review by EOD 3) ellie — schedule call and send pre-read. I'll track in the account board under Nimbus - Renewal/Onboarding. :white_check_mark:

ellie: Got it. I'll update the ticket DPA-8712 with meeting notes and next steps after the call.

mike: Thanks team — looks good.
